cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick the Prize
cards.instruction: Make them choose which reward, principle, or relationship matters most when not everything can be kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Choose the trophy ceremony or our anniversary dinner. They're at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then you're choosing the trophy and postponing us. Say which.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It could be a short ceremony.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you leave before your name is called? That's the choice.

mechanism: A assumes authority to define what B proposed compromise really chooses, forcing an explicit priority when a reward and relationship or group benefit cannot all be retained.
confusable: D200 raises stakes; D202 exposes an existing incompatibility and demands which value wins rather than adding a larger cost.
comparison: Anniversary timing forces ceremony-versus-relationship priority; prize money forces personal retention-versus-team funding and who pays.
seedUse: Read both full cards and all four seeds. Preserve B compromise attempts and actual scarcity, avoiding invented reasons every compromise must be impossible.
